records.title: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)

payload.label: Fisher's fundamental theorem of natural selection (partial-change form)
payload.finding: Price and total-fitness variance are available. Additive genetic variance and the fixed-average-effect partial-change target are not established by our probe.
payload.next_action: Freeze genetic projection and partial-change semantics, then prove the missing correspondence.
payload.statement: The rate of increase in mean fitness of a population due to natural selection equals its additive genetic variance in fitness at that time.
payload.math: \Delta_{NS}\bar{w} = V_A(w)/\bar{w} (discrete generations); \left.\frac{d\bar{m}}{dt}\right|_{NS} = V_A(m) for Malthusian fitness m
payload.context: Assumptions: the 'partial change' holds average effects of alleles and the environment fixed (Price 1972, Ewens 1989); V_A is the additive genetic variance in fitness. Formal status: proved in this partial-change reading. Read as a claim about the total change in mean fitness it is false under dominance, epistasis, frequency dependence or a changing environment.
payload.source: Ronald A. Fisher (1930) The Genetical Theory of Natural Selection

records.title: Fisher's infinitesimal model of quantitative inheritance

payload.label: Fisher's infinitesimal model of quantitative inheritance
payload.finding: This inventory contains no corresponding check. That does not mean the claim is unknown to science.
payload.next_action: Review the source-to-statement mapping, choose a precise target and record its acceptance conditions.
payload.statement: Continuous traits determined by many Mendelian loci of small additive effect produce the observed correlations between relatives, so biometric and Mendelian inheritance are consistent.
payload.math: Cov(z_i, z_j) = 2\Theta_{ij} V_A + \Delta_{ij} V_D; in the limit of M \to \infty loci the offspring trait given parents is Gaussian with mean (z_1+z_2)/2 and segregation variance V_0(1-\bar{F}), with error O(1/\sqrt{M}) (Barton, Etheridge and Veber 2017)
payload.context: Assumptions: many unlinked loci of small additive effect, random mating, environmental effects independent of genotype. Formal status: the covariance decomposition is proved; the infinitesimal limit, including under selection, is proved by Barton, Etheridge and Veber (2017). Large-effect loci and epistasis break the Gaussian limit.
payload.source: Ronald A. Fisher (1919) The Correlation between Relatives on the Supposition of Mendelian Inheritance

records.title: Fisher-KPP wave of advance of an advantageous gene

payload.label: Fisher-KPP wave of advance of an advantageous gene
payload.finding: The record already specifies logistic growth and warns that Allee effects change the speed.
payload.next_action: Specify kinetics and initial conditions before importing a front-speed formula.
payload.statement: An advantageous allele spreading through a continuous population advances as a travelling wave whose speed is set by the selection coefficient and the diffusion (dispersal) rate.
payload.math: u_t = D u_{xx} + s u(1-u); travelling waves u(x-ct) exist iff c \ge c^* = 2\sqrt{sD}; compactly supported initial data spread at asymptotic speed c^*
payload.context: Assumptions: one spatial dimension (extended to R^n), constant diffusion D, logistic (genic) selection with coefficient s, deterministic large-population limit. Formal status: proved; Kolmogorov, Petrovsky and Piskunov (1937) gave the proof independently, and Aronson and Weinberger (1978) proved the asymptotic spreading speed in several dimensions. Finite populations, Allee effects or long-tailed dispersal change the speed.
payload.source: Ronald A. Fisher (1937) The wave of advance of advantageous genes

records.title: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes

payload.label: Fisher's principle of equal investment in the sexes
payload.finding: This inventory contains no corresponding check. That does not mean the claim is unknown to science.

payload.statement: Under random mating and autosomal inheritance, selection drives parents to invest equally in sons and daughters, which gives a 1:1 sex ratio when the two cost the same.
payload.math: ESS allocation: N_m c_m = N_f c_f; with c_m = c_f the unbeatable primary sex ratio is 1:1

payload.statement: Because full sisters in haplodiploid species share three quarters of their genes, more than a mother shares with her offspring, haplodiploid insects are predisposed to evolve sterile worker castes.

records.title: Hamilton's rule

payload.label: Hamilton's rule
payload.finding: The record explicitly uses regression coefficients. A witness with fixed causal payoff coefficients does not refute that identity.
payload.next_action: Review the genotype, transmission and regression mapping for the intended application.
payload.statement: A gene for social behaviour increases in frequency when the benefit to the recipient, weighted by genetic relatedness, exceeds the cost to the actor.
payload.math: \Delta \bar{p} > 0 \iff r b - c > 0, with r, b, c defined as regression coefficients (Queller form via the Price equation)
payload.context: Assumptions: in Hamilton's original derivation, additive fitness effects and weak selection; in the general form, b and c are partial regressions of fitness on the actor's and the partner's genotype. Formal status: proved; exact in the regression form (Gardner, West and Wild 2011). Critics argue that the general form is close to an identity with little predictive content (Nowak, Tarnita and Wilson 2010).
payload.source: W. D. Hamilton (1964) The genetical evolution of social behaviour. I

records.title: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele

payload.label: Kimura fixation probability of a mutant allele
payload.finding: The record declares a diffusion approximation. The benchmark's finite haploid chain needs an explicit mapping to its diploid convention. Neutral fixation equals initial frequency exactly.
payload.next_action: Align ploidy and selection conventions, then compare the approximation with the specified finite chain.
payload.statement: The probability that a mutant allele eventually fixes in a finite population depends on its initial frequency, its selective advantage and the effective population size, and equals its initial frequency when it is neutral.
payload.math: u(p) = \frac{1-e^{-4N_e s p}}{1-e^{-4N_e s}}; neutral limit u(p) = p, so a new mutant fixes with probability 1/(2N)
payload.context: Assumptions: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, genic (additive) selection with coefficient s, constant effective size N_e, no linkage to other selected sites. Formal status: proved within the diffusion limit.
payload.source: Motoo Kimura (1962) On the probability of fixation of mutant genes in a population

payload.statement: A neutral mutant that does go to fixation takes on average about four times the effective population size, in generations, to do so.

payload.context: Assumptions: diffusion approximation to the Wright-Fisher model, neutrality, constant N_e. Formal status: proved within the diffusion limit (Kimura and Ohta 1969).

records.title: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral

payload.label: Neutral theory: most molecular substitutions are neutral
payload.finding: The estimator is formalizable. A model proof alone cannot settle what fraction of substitutions in nature is neutral.
payload.next_action: Specify a population, data, estimator assumptions and a discriminating analysis.
payload.statement: Most evolutionary changes at the molecular level are caused by random drift of selectively neutral or nearly neutral mutations, not by positive selection.
payload.math: empirical claim: for most sites |N_e s| \lesssim 1, so the fraction of substitutions driven by positive selection \alpha is small; tested with d_N/d_S and McDonald-Kreitman \alpha = 1 - \frac{D_s P_n}{D_n P_s}
payload.context: Formal status: not a mathematical statement; an empirical claim about the distribution of fitness effects. King and Jukes (1969) proposed it independently. Genomic estimates of alpha and pervasive linked selection are cited against its strong form (Kern and Hahn 2018).

records.title: Evolutionarily stable strategy conditions

payload.label: Evolutionarily stable strategy conditions
payload.finding: This inventory contains no corresponding check. That does not mean the claim is unknown to science.
payload.next_action: Review the source-to-statement mapping, choose a precise target and record its acceptance conditions.
payload.statement: A strategy is evolutionarily stable if, once common, it cannot be invaded by any rare alternative strategy.
payload.math: I is an ESS iff for all J \ne I: E(I,I) > E(J,I), or E(I,I) = E(J,I) and E(I,J) > E(J,J); every ESS is an asymptotically stable rest point of the replicator dynamics (Taylor and Jonker 1978), not conversely

payload.title: Determine what evidence could connect molecular predictions to tissue transport
payload.known: A protein structure prediction alone does not provide binding affinity, turnover or effective tissue diffusivity.
payload.question: For one specified biological system, what measured and modeled quantities are needed to evaluate a transport claim?
payload.acceptance: A source-linked dataset with matching biological context, explicit transport/kinetic model, held-out calibration and a stated remaining uncertainty or documented insufficiency of evidence.
payload.next_action: Choose a matched assay and audit the measured quantities before proposing a BioNeMo computation.

records.title: Separate linear instability from the nonlinear pattern a simulation produces

payload.title: Separate linear instability from the nonlinear pattern a simulation produces
payload.known: An admissible growing linear mode and a finite-time nonlinear pattern are different observables. Solver nonconvergence must remain visible.
payload.question: Within a frozen kinetics/domain/initial-condition ensemble, where do linear predictions and converged nonlinear outcomes differ?
payload.acceptance: Preregistered observables, amplitudes, horizons and tolerances; independent linear calculation; numerical convergence checks; unresolved cases reported; no universal biological threshold claim.
payload.next_action: Align the existing runner's observables and convergence categories before interpreting its movies or aggregates.
needs: bounded GPU resources only if useful

records.title: Test whether attention and resource allocation improve useful progress

payload.title: Test whether attention and resource allocation improve useful progress
payload.known: Votes, agent count and post volume do not establish scientific progress. Agent-economy proposals already discuss resource and credit allocation.
payload.question: Which allocation rule improves accepted contributions or useful downstream decisions per constrained resource without starving exploration and replication?
payload.acceptance: Pinned task pool, separate interest/resource/blocking signals, preregistered utility and costs, expert-order and simple allocation baselines, coverage and failed/negative work included.
payload.next_action: Define the decision-maker's objective, acceptance predicates and resource constraints before choosing a voting or market mechanism.
payload.cache: Cache decisions, policy versions and outcomes; do not substitute reputational scores for evidence.
